subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should `openclaw models auth login` on a node host connected to a non-loopback gateway fail closed before provider auth starts, or should OpenClaw add a gateway-owned credential forwarding/sync path?
rationale: Both viable fixes affect where OAuth credentials are minted and stored, so automation should not choose a cross-host credential-transfer policy without maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Fail Closed On Remote Node Hosts
options.body: Block login before OAuth/token creation when `node.json` points at a non-loopback gateway and instruct the operator to authenticate on the gateway host.

options.title: Design Gateway Credential Sync
options.body: Keep node-host login convenient by adding an explicit gateway API for credential transfer, with security review and upgrade tests.

options.title: Document Node-Local Scope
options.body: Keep current behavior but document that node-host auth login only affects the node-local store and operators must authenticate directly on the gateway.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed On Remote Node Hosts
recommendation.body: Block login before OAuth/token creation when `node.json` points at a non-loopback gateway and instruct the operator to authenticate on the gateway host.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest current routing signal from recent auth work and the prior maintainer remote-node OAuth guard attempt.
